label: caiso 11 ixshape probe
definition: (PROBE — informative negative result, NOT a keeper) caiso-10 baseline + --interchange-shaping (shape the priced node by the measured EIA-930 diurnal net-interchange envelope: import overnight / export midday). HYPOTHESIS: forcing midday exports of the solar glut, once the export sink saturates, makes surplus curtail renewables at -$20 and unlocks the negative midday tail. RESULT: it DID unlock negatives in 2023 (12 hrs, min -$20) and 2025 (1 hr) — the export->curtail mechanism is real — but 2024 stayed at 0. The cost is a NET REGRESSION: the shaping caps GROSS import availability to the NET-import envelope (net << gross because CAISO imports and exports simultaneously), starving baseload imports (2024 32.1->17.4 TWh vs actual 32.4) and substituting gas (+14 to +17 TWh, 2024 70.9->85.0 vs EIA-923 67.7), which pushes the MEAN LMP UP (2024 $54.2->$61.4; actual ~$33) — wrong direction. Diurnal swing improved (2024 1492->1918 MW) but still far short of actual 4596. DIAGNOSIS: the EXPORT half (force midday export) is physically right and unlocks the tail; the IMPORT-CAP half is the regression (net/gross conflation). NEXT (caiso-12): export-only shaping — keep the forced midday export, drop the import-availability cap so baseload imports stay realistic and gas doesn't inflate.
